# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-15 (Extended v123)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Autumn Year 4, evening—crisis at Gorbeau house escalating rapidly)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens; le Petit-Picpus convent; M. Gillenormand's residences; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick, Wilholt). **Current environmental**: Smoke from chimneys lies flat over fields; frost silvered hedges overnight; bell for vespers rings thinly across roofs; light went early; icy breeze; wind off water carries salt/tar scent; gulls quarrel over fish heads; rain threatens; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall; cart loaded with turnips creaked past well.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid, sordid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, obscene charcoal sketches, repulsive moisture. Fireplace with brazier filled burning charcoal (glowing hot, red with blue flame), pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (sleeping woman/child, eagle, Napoleon on blue column). **Wooden panel—Battle of Waterloo painting: sergeant rescuer (Thénardier) carrying colonel victim (Pontmercy) amid smoke.** Two heaps: old iron/ropes and rope-ladder with wooden rungs and two hooks. Verdigris candlestick with burning candle.

## Crisis at Peak: M. Leblanc's Extraordinary Escape
**Sequence of events (evening)**: M. Leblanc initially overturned chair and table, moved toward window with prodigious agility. Six robust fists seized him—three "chimney-builders" dragged him back. Thénardier woman wound hands in his hair. Herculean struggle: M. Leblanc knocked old man tumbling, overthrew two more with backward hand sweeps. Four others seized him by both arms and back of neck.

**M. Leblanc bound with ropes.** Despite binding, surrounded, half plunged in grave, M. Leblanc remained impassive—soul inaccessible to terror. Preserved silence, carried precaution of forgetting anxiety for own life. **Marius found this superbly melancholy visage and extraordinary composure deeply troubling.**

**Thénardier's metamorphosis**: Transformed from ferocious robber into polished negotiator—moderated language, subdued, crafty, reserved, choice diction. Marius difficult recognizing tiger converted into lawyer. **Thénardier's scheme**: Wife will dress as before and hunt up "the Lark" (Cosette) with letter from M. Leblanc. Girl will follow into carriage. Outside barrier, trap with two horses waits. Young lady will alight from fiacre; Thénardier's comrade will enter other vehicle with her; wife returns to report completion. **Threat**: "If you have me arrested, my comrade will give a turn of his thumb to the Lark, that's all." **Deliberate name avoidance**: Thénardier avoided naming girl—precaution of clever man.

**M. Leblanc's address demanded**: Thénardier instructed M. Leblanc to write letter addressed "Mademoiselle Fabre" to his house. "I know that you live a long distance from here, near Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas, because you go to mass there every day, but I don't know in what street."

**M. Leblanc's extraordinary act (turning point)**: Before seven men could collect senses, M. Leblanc bent down into fireplace, stretched out hand to brazier, straightened himself up. **Brandished above his head the red-hot chisel, emitting threatening glow**—almost free and in formidable attitude. Thénardier, female Thénardier, and ruffians huddled in amazement at extremity of hovel, stared in stupefaction.

**Means of escape**: Prisoner had coin piece on person when searched; contrived to conceal it in hand; having right hand free, unscrewed it and used as saw to cut cords—explaining faint noise Marius had observed.

**Marius's response**: Reeled in utter horror. Very ruffians shuddered. Hardly muscle of old man's face contracted. While red-hot iron sank into smoking wound, **impassive and almost august, he fixed on Thénardier his beautiful glance, in which there was no hatred, and where suffering vanished in serene majesty.**

## Javert's Ambush Deployment
**Status (Autumn Year 4, evening)**: Tall man, square face, thin firm mouth, thick gray ferocious whiskers. **Action timeline**: Received report from Marius regarding Jondrette ambush. Gave Marius two small steel pistols (each loaded two balls). Instructed Marius to hide, watch through wall hole, fire when crisis reached peak. Entered hovel, positioned for ambush.

**Javert's operational sequence (evening)**: At nightfall, posted men and went into ambush himself between trees of Rue de la Barrière-des-Gobelins facing Gorbeau house, other side of boulevard. Began operations by opening "his pockets," dropping into it two young girls charged with keeping watch on approaches. Only "caged" Azelma—Éponine disappeared, not at post, could not seize her. Made a point and bent ear waiting for signal agreed upon (pistol-shot). Comings and goings of fiacres greatly agitated him. At last grew impatient. Sure there was "a nest there," sure of being in "luck," having recognized many ruffians who entered, decided to go upstairs without waiting for pistol-shot. **Took action before Marius fired.**

**Ruffians' response to Javert's arrival**: Terrified ruffians flung themselves on arms abandoned in corners at moment of flight. In less than a second, seven men had grouped themselves in attitude of defence—one with meat-axe, another with key, another with bludgeon, rest with shears, pincers, hammers. Thénardier had knife in fist. **Thénardier woman snatched enormous paving-stone from angle of window (daughters' ottoman), hurled at Javert's head. Javert ducked; stone passed over him, struck wall behind, knocked off huge piece of plastering, rebounded across hovel (almost empty), rested at Javert's feet.**

**M. Leblanc's escape during chaos**: Door was guarded, but window was not. As soon as released from bonds and while Javert drawing up report, took advantage of confusion, crowd, darkness, moment when general attention diverted from him, to dash out of window.

## Marius Pontmercy: Crisis of Conscience (Unresolved)
**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen. **Now recognized**: Thénardier depicted in Waterloo painting—sergeant who rescued father at Waterloo.

**Unprecedented perplexity (evening crisis)**: For last hour had two voices in conscience—one enjoining him to respect father's testament, other crying to rescue prisoner. Two voices continued uninterrupted struggle tormenting him to agony. Up to that moment cherished vague hope of reconciling two duties, but nothing within limits of possibility presented itself. **Had not time for deliberation—scene hastening to catastrophe. He was on verge of swooning. Knees gave way beneath him. Last possibility of doubt vanished. Certainly was Thénardier of the will.**

**Critical moral dilemma**: Everything depended on Marius. Unknown to themselves, he held all beings in his hand. If he fired pistol, M. Leblanc saved, Thénardier lost; if he did not fire, M. Leblanc sacrificed. Remorse awaited him either case. Father once saved by Thénardier at Waterloo—sergeant rescued colonel. Yet M. Leblanc now victim of Thénardier's ambush. Moral obligation to both: honor father's will AND prevent crime against innocent man and Cosette's father. **Crisis of conscience at absolute peak.**

**Current state**: A sort of horrible fascination held him nailed to post. Almost incapable of movement or reflection. He waited, in hope of some incident, no matter of what nature, since he could not collect his thoughts and did not know upon what course to decide.

## Girl (Cosette) and M. Leblanc Identity
**Girl identity clarified**: Handkerchief bore letters U. F., which meant Urbain Fabre, not Ursule. M. Leblanc is Monsieur Fabre—the girl's biological father. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. **Marius now recognizes**: The "girl" he worshipped for six months is Cosette, whom he encountered again miraculously in hovel as charitable visitor with M. Leblanc. She is also being held captive by Thénardier's scheme.

## Jean Valjean
Valjean integrated as convent assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence.

## English Provincial Towns: Mundane Activities
**Stenworth and Prydenridge families**: Pelde Stenson, Davus Stenworth, Fewyn Stenworth, Havus Stenworth (fell asleep in chair before fire caught; asked if it will rain), Dalis (daughter born). Yera Stenworth, Nerine Prydenridge, Luvie Prydenridge, Zavus Prydenridge, Vesmira Thornmere, Wenelle Lindmere (gave up idleness, took work as chandler). Isric Thornmere. **Fewyn Stenworth argued with carter over price of sack of oats** (repeated twice—plan to pay debt to Prydenridge family never begun). Daily activities: sorting old letters, mending torn sleeves, scrubbing steps, humming childhood tunes. Conversations: weather, harvest, lame horse, rain, river up, price of salt. **Peten Haskick broke faith with Luwyn Brackick; promised work (pay old debt owed to Prydenridge family) never begun.** **Kadrek went along to live in Wilholt. Only daughter of Zalis Corrley left Torton and settled in Wilholt.** Baker's boy late again; line at oven grew long. Children chased hoop down lane, shrieking. Almanac read aloud.

## Historical Context (1831-1832)
Two years immediately connected with Revolution of July form peculiar and striking moment of history. Rise like two mountains midway between preceding and following years. Possess revolutionary grandeur. Social masses, civilization's assizes, century-old profiles of ancient French formation appear and disappear amidst storm clouds of systems, passions, theories. Nation asks nothing but repose, thirsts for peace, has ambition to be small. Great events, hazards, adventures, great men—thank God, seen enough, heaped higher than heads. Would exchange Caesar for Prusias, Napoleon for King of Yvetot. Marched since daybreak, reached evening of long toilsome day. Made first change with Mirabeau, second with Robespierre, third with Bonaparte; worn out. Each demands bed. House of Bourbon returned to France when Napoleon fell with fatal simplicity, believed it bestowed and could take back charter rights. Did not suspect roots of French society not fixed in Bourbons but in nations. Bourbons were illustrious and bleeding knot in history, but no longer principal element of destiny, necessary base of politics. France could get along without them; had done without them for twenty-two years. Never had princes been so blind in presence of facts and divine authority contained therein.
